comments.body:
Implementation note — the recorded "28 -> 30" corpus numbers are stale, and the test asserts the
delta instead.

Measured on `origin/main` (aaf71639b8) with the repo venv, `provider_parity.select_corpus(
eligible_cases())`:

- BEFORE (container cases payload-less): 128 eligible, **26** in the selected corpus
- AFTER  (all 12 cases carry `children`): 140 eligible, **28** in the selected corpus

The +12 eligible / +2 selected delta is exactly what the ticket predicted; only the absolute
totals differ, because the spec set has changed since story 0d76 recorded 28/30. The container
spec contributes exactly 2 because `select_corpus` takes the FIRST gold-block and FIRST
gold-advisory case per spec — and those two are precisely `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` and
`G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar`, the two cases 0d76 measured raising on both arms at
every epoch.

So the new test in `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` asserts
`len(select_corpus(eligible)) == len(select_corpus(eligible_without_container)) + 2` plus
`sorted(labels) == ["advisory", "block"]`, rather than a hard-coded total that would break the
next time an unrelated eval spec is added. The description's AC line naming "30" should be read
as that +2 delta.

On the decision the original AC asked for: I did NOT re-open it. The project's own record
settles it — `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` states in its own comment that "a container
criterion with no `children` payload is a fixture error, not a silent pass", and
`plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` is the same kind of spec shipping the payload, with the
shape documented in its header. Adding payloads is following that record, not choosing between
open options. Every `children` list is transcribed from the case's existing `input` prose, so no
`input`, `expect`, `criterion`, `mode`, `note` or `gold_set` line changed.

compiled_state.description:
# Container eval fixtures without a `children` payload cannot be run by `run_case`

## Problem

`eval_solver._run_criterion_case` raises for a CONTAINER criterion (G3 / G4 / decomp-shape)
whose case carries no non-empty `children` list — the criterion runs `pass1_container` over a
(parent, children, sibling-roster) decomposition, not inline text. ALL 12 cases in
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carry only `input` (the parent plan)
and no `children`, so none can be executed through `run_case`.
`plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` cases DO carry `children` and are the working precedent.

## Evidence (measured, story 0d76)

In the live provider-parity run, `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` and
`G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar` raised
`ValueError: container criterion 'G3' needs a non-empty children list in the eval fixture` on
BOTH arms at ALL 3 epochs, before any model call, on both class slots. They contributed nothing
but error counts. `provider_parity._runnable` now excludes them, so the parity corpus is 28
items rather than 30. (Only those two surface because `select_corpus` takes the FIRST
gold-block and FIRST gold-advisory case per spec; the other ten are equally unrunnable.)

## The decision, and why it is already settled by the project's own record

The original AC asked whether to add `children` payloads or to document the cases as runnable
only through `pass1_container` directly. The repo already answers this, so this ticket does NOT
re-open it:

- `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` states the contract in its own comment: *"A container
  criterion with no `children` payload is a **fixture error**, not a silent pass."* The raise is
  deliberately loud precisely so the fixture gets fixed.
- `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` is the same kind of spec with the payload present, and
  documents the shape in its header: *"Container criteria run over a (parent, children)
  decomposition, so each case carries the parent plan as `input` and the children as a
  `children:` list."*
- `_run_criterion_case` drives the SAME `pass1_container` fan-out the real gate uses, so a
  `children`-carrying fixture IS the "runnable through `pass1_container`" path — the second
  option is not a different capability, only a decision to leave the corpus smaller.

So: add the payloads. No new capability, no contract change, no code change.

## Approach

Add a `children:` list to each of the 12 cases in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml`, each entry
`{ticket_id, title, description}`, matching the decomp-shape shape exactly.

The children are **transcribed, not invented**: every case's existing `input` prose already
names its child set (e.g. `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar`: "Its children cover the importer, the API,
and the UI — but NO child addresses idempotency"; `G4-R-ordering-violation-snap`: "Child A
deletes the legacy payments column; child B still reads it"). Each `children` list makes exactly
those children explicit and adds nothing the `input` does not already assert, so the gold label
(`expect`) of every case is unchanged by construction.

`sibling_roster` is deliberately NOT pinned per case: `_run_criterion_case` falls back to
`build_sibling_roster(children)`, the ONE shared builder, so eval fixtures see the same roster
shape production does.

No source change: `provider_parity._runnable` already admits any container case with a non-empty
`children` list, so `eligible_cases` picks the fixed cases up unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` — add `children:` to all 12 dataset
  cases. `prompt`, `model`, `epochs`, `gate`, `scorers`, `tolerance`, every `input`, every
  `expect`/`criterion`/`corpus`/`note`/`mode`, and the whole `gold_set` are UNCHANGED.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — `test_container_cases_without_a_children_payload_are_excluded`
  ends with `assert all(i.spec != "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`, using
  the container spec as the witness that the exclusion rule is non-vacuous. Once the fixtures are
  fixed that witness is false. The RULE stays pinned (the `_runnable` unit assertions in the same
  test already prove it non-vacuously on synthetic cases); only the stale witness line is
  replaced by its inverse — that the container spec is now eligible.

## Testing

- The load-bearing assertion is that every container case in `eligible_cases()` carries a
  non-empty `children` payload AND that the container spec is now represented — i.e. the ticket's
  own AC becomes an executable test rather than a manual check. This is added to
  `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` in place of the stale witness line.
- A fixture-shape test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` pins that EVERY dataset case in
  `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a non-empty `children` list whose entries each have
  `ticket_id`/`title`/`description` — so a future case added without a payload fails CI instead
  of silently dropping out of the corpus (which is exactly how this bug went unnoticed).
- No live model call is needed: `_runnable` / `eligible_cases` / spec loading are all offline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every dataset case in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a
      non-empty `children:` list whose entries each have `ticket_id`, `title` and `description`;
      pinned by a new test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` that fails if any case lacks
      one.
- [ ] `provider_parity.eligible_cases()` picks the container cases up with NO change to
      `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py` or `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`; verified
      by `git diff --stat` showing neither file modified, and by a test asserting
      `any(i.spec == "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`.
- [ ] `len(select_corpus(eligible_cases()))` is 30 (up from 28) — the container spec contributes
      its first gold-block and first gold-advisory case again.
- [ ] Every container item in `eligible_cases()` satisfies `item.case["children"]`; the existing
      exclusion RULE remains pinned by the `_runnable` assertions
      (`not _runnable("G3", {"input": ...})`, `_runnable("G3", {"children": [...]})`).
- [ ] Each case's `expect` label is unchanged and each `children` list is entailed by that case's
      existing `input` prose (no new scenario invented); reviewable by diffing that no `input`,
      `expect`, `criterion`, or `gold_set` line changed.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green with the worktree venv on PATH.

replace the stale exclusion witness with the eligibility assertion
